find: When asked which commandment was the greatest, he said that loving God with your whole heart is the first and greatest commandment, and that a second is like it: love your neighbour as yourself (Luke 10:25–37).
replace: In Matthew 22:37–39 Jesus calls loving God with your whole heart the first and greatest commandment, and says the second is like it: love your neighbour as yourself. In Luke 10:25–28 an expert in the law gives Jesus those same two commands, and Jesus tells him he has answered correctly.
note: F1: the 'first and greatest / the second is like it' wording is Matthew 22:37-39. In Luke 10 the expert in the law says it, not Jesus. The Good Samaritan still follows in Luke 10:29-37.

find: Jesus taught his followers to ask God to forgive them “as we forgive those who sin against us” (Matthew 6:5–13).
replace: Jesus taught his followers to ask God, “Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors” (Matthew 6:12). Churches usually say this line as “forgive us our sins as we forgive those who sin against us”.
note: F2: the quoted words are the modern liturgical Lord's Prayer, not the Bible text at Matthew 6. NIV Matthew 6:12 restored, with the familiar church wording kept.

find: The Marian Shrine of Cardigan, also a historic British pilgrimage destination, draws Catholic pilgrims who come for prayer and reflection.
replace: Two sites are set for study on this course. Walsingham in Norfolk is England’s main shrine to Mary: a noblewoman had a vision there in 1061 and built a copy of the house in Nazareth where Mary was told she would bear Jesus. Anglican, Catholic and Orthodox pilgrims all visit today. Taizé in Burgundy, France, is a monastic community founded by Brother Roger in 1940 whose brothers come from both Catholic and Protestant traditions. More than 100,000 young people go there each year for simple chanted worship and shared silence.
